meta.title: Dunjunz, official disc (Model B side): the game
meta.description:
Annotated disassembly of the game file `Dun1`, which contains the level loader `Coder`.

## How Dun1 is laid out

| In Dun1 | Runs at | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| &2000-&2FFF | in place | The exit animation, `drop_key`, `object_free_map`, doors and keys, sprites |
| &3000-&473F | &08C0-&1FFF | The game core, copied down by Coder |
| &5000-&51AF | in place | `coder_start` (Coder), its commands and VDU tables |
| &51B0-&55AF | &0400-&07FF | The keyboard-only image of page &04-&07 |
| &55B0-&59AF | &0400-&07FF | The same with `joystick_bytev` at &0780 |
| &6E80-&7FFF | in place | Heroes, missiles, objects, monsters, `workspace_template`, `wrch_handler` |

Coder is also a file of its own, `Coder` (&5000-&59AF), identical to
those bytes of Dun1.

## Memory map in play

| Range | Contents |
|---|---|
| &0000-&03FF | Zero page, stack and MOS workspace; the game's zero page is &70-&8F; &0287 is the MOS BREAK intercept |
| &0400-&07FF | One of the two images: score overflow, `decrypt_level`, the hero menu, `remove_absent_heroes` (and `joystick_bytev`) |
| &08B0-&08BF | Page &08 state that survives the reset between levels: `hero_score_ten_thousands`, `hero_absent`, `levels_started`, `level_digits` |
| &08C0-&0CFF | `plot_sprite`, `screen_address`, per-hero tables and scores, `room_walls` at &0C00; copied only for the first level, so the heroes carry over |
| &0D00-&1FFF | Page &0D's per-level workspace, `game_entry`, the level loop, the status panel, the victory sequence, `start_level`, `check_level`, the BREAK intercepts, the font, sprites, `update_game`, `play_level` |
| &2000-&2FFF | The exit animation, doors and keys, sprites |
| &3000-&6E7F | Screen (25 character rows in play); Dun1's stored copies lie here until the screen is cleared |
| &6B00-&6DAF | The level file, in the screen's bottom rows |
| &6E80-&7FFF | Heroes, missiles, objects, monsters, `workspace_template`, `wrch_handler` |

## From power-on to play

1. Booted on a Model B, the other side's BOOT asks for the disc to be
   turned over and runs `*DUNJUNZ` (its own listing). That sets page &08
   (`levels_started` 0, `level_digits` "0 ", every hero playing), shows
   the title screen, arms the BREAK intercept with a JMP to &15B5 and runs
   `*CODER` with VDU output disabled.
2. `coder_start` (&5000) disables ESCAPE, cancels the BREAK intercept,
   counts the level in `levels_started` and `level_digits`, and blanks
   the display. It `*LOAD`s Dun1 (over itself), then `LEVELnn` to &6B00,
   or for level 25 `STONES`, whose end is level 25. It copies the
   keyboard image, or the joystick image if ADC channel 1 reads &80, to
   &0400, and points BYTEV at `joystick_bytev` if a second read says so.
   It shows 23 rows, copies the game core (from &0D00 only, after the
   first level) and jumps to `game_entry` at &0D31, leaving
   `levels_started` in `level_count_copy` (&8E).
3. `game_entry` sets the bell, saves WRCHV in `saved_wrchv` and points it
   at `wrch_handler`, and sets `level_number` from &8E. On the first level
   it resets the heroes and runs `hero_menu`; on later ones it goes
   straight to `level_loop`.
4. `level_loop` sets `monster_start_hit_points` from `levels_started` and
   calls `start_level`, which runs steps 5 to 7.
5. `clear_text_for_level` clears rows 0-22 only, so the level file in rows
   23-24 survives.
6. `check_level` decrypts the level and checks it against
   `level_checksums` (`decrypt_level` resets the machine on a mismatch),
   then widens `clear_text_area`'s window to all 25 rows.
7. `unpack_level`, `reset_workspace` and `reset_monsters` set up play; the
   screen is cleared and set to 25 rows, and `draw_view_frames` draws the
   frames and the four views.
8. `draw_status_panel` and `remove_absent_heroes` finish the screen, and
   `play_level` runs the level until no hero is left in play.
9. Every dead hero gets their starting attributes back. If any hero
   survived, `next_level_by_reset` arms the BREAK intercept with a JMP to
   `next_level_intercept` and resets the machine; on the intercept's
   second call, once the filing system is back, it selects MODE 2 and runs
   `*CODER` again, which loads the next level (step 2). If all four died,
   the game-over message is shown for up to 5.8 seconds or until a key,
   and `restart_by_reset` resets the machine into `restart_intercept`,
   which runs `*DUNJUNZ` (step 1). A hero reaching the Chalice on level 25
   is caught by `check_for_victory`, which plays `victory_sequence`,
   prints the ending message, waits for a key and resets the machine
   through the RESET vector.

subroutines.name: plot_sprite
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite
subroutines.description:
Copy sprite sprite_number to the screen with its top-left corner at byte column plot_x, pixel row plot_y. 

The four sprite tables, indexed by sprite number, give the address of its data and its size: sprite_width bytes across (two MODE 2 pixels to a byte) by sprite_height pixel rows. The data is stored row by row and is written over the screen contents without masking, so a sprite's black pixels erase what was there, and there is no clipping. The screen is laid out like MODE 2 with 640-byte character rows from &3000, so successive bytes of a sprite row are 8 bytes apart, and each pixel row starts one byte below the last, or 640-7 bytes on when it crosses into the next character row. screen_ptr walks across each row, row_start_ptr remembers where the row began, and sprite_data_ptr walks through the data; Y stays 0. sprite_width and sprite_height are left holding the sprite's size.

subroutines.name: screen_address
subroutines.title: Calculate a screen address
subroutines.description: Set screen_ptr to the screen address of byte column plot_x on pixel row plot_y: &3000 + 640 x (plot_y DIV 8) + (plot_y MOD 8) + 8 x plot_x. plot_sprite calls it once per sprite, for the top-left byte. The multiplication by 640 is done with a table inside MOS 1.20 (mos_row_offsets, two bytes per character row, high byte first), so this only works with that MOS. The high byte of 8 x plot_x is plot_x DIV 32, taken from plot_x's top three bits with four ROLs.

subroutines.name: wrch_handler
subroutines.title: WRCHV handler: print letters and digits in the game font
subroutines.description: Installed on WRCHV while the game runs. A letter (either case) or a digit is printed in the game's own font: its eight-byte glyph is copied over the definition of character 128 (user_char_128) and character 128 is printed instead. Every other character is printed unchanged. Both paths finish in the MOS 1.20 OSWRCH routine at mos_oswrch_default, jumped to directly rather than through the WRCHV value saved at start-up. Lower-case letters share the capitals' glyphs. The handler keeps the character in plot_x, the sprite plotter's zero-page column, and it looks at every byte alone, with no notion of a VDU sequence: a VDU parameter byte that falls in '0'-'9', 'A'-'Z' or 'a'-'z' is sent as &80 too.

subroutines.name: add_thousand_points
subroutines.title: Add 1000 to a hero's score
subroutines.description: Carry a point into the thousands of hero X's score. add_ten_points calls it whenever the hundreds digit passes 9, and on return its draw_score redraws the four large digits (thousands to units) in the hero's panel section. The panel has room for only those four, so when the thousands digit passes 9 it goes back to 0 and the ten-thousands digit (hero_score_ten_thousands, a small digit sprite) goes up. That digit sticks at 9, so beyond 99,999 the large digits wrap while the small one stays at 9. Each change of the ten-thousands digit is drawn at draw_ten_thousands: the small digit &18 rows below the hero's panel row, under the score, followed by four of sprite &71. Sprite &71, the small 8, is a solid bar two pixels wide, the same shape a small 0 would have, so the line reads as a small N0000. remove_absent_heroes enters at draw_ten_thousands with the digit in A, to redraw the line on the fresh screen of each level. Uses plot_x, plot_y and sprite_number.

subroutines.name: reset_hero
subroutines.title: Give a hero their starting attributes
subroutines.description: Undo everything hero X has gained: set their missile limit, missile damage and health lost per hit (hero_max_missiles, hero_missile_damage, hero_damage_taken) from the starting tables at &0F80, and their score to 0000 with no ten-thousands digit. It is called for every hero when a game starts, and by level_loop for each hero who died (or was not playing) when a level ends, so a dead hero comes back on the next level as new, while survivors keep their scores and the gains from objects. Health and position are not set here: reset_workspace restores those for every hero at each level. The units digit is set one below 0 because draw_status_panel draws the score by adding a point.

subroutines.name: draw_status_panel
subroutines.title: Draw the status panel
subroutines.description:
Draw each hero's section of the status panel, the column to the right of the views, Ranger at the top to Fighter at the bottom. level_loop calls it once per level, after start_level has drawn the fresh screen and before remove_absent_heroes. 

The health and score are drawn by the routines play uses to change them: lose_health_point takes a point from the template's health of 99 + 1, so every hero starts every level on 99, and add_point adds one to the score, which a hero just reset has one below 0000. So a hero who survived the last level, and kept their score, gains a point here at every new level. Then, through plot_panel_sprite, which places each sprite relative to the hero's panel row (hero_panel_y): the face and the shield on the section's top row, with the armour rating (10 - health lost per hit) as a small digit on the shield; the missile damage as a small digit; and one missile icon per missile allowed in flight, three rows apart, beside the health. The keys, the boots icon and the ten-thousands digit are drawn elsewhere. panel_hero is the hero being drawn; count holds the icons' end row.

subroutines.name: plot_panel_sprite
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite in a hero's panel section
subroutines.description: Plot sprite A at byte column X and pixel row Y + hero_panel_y - 14 for the hero panel_hero, the one draw_status_panel is drawing. Row 0 of a section is thus 14 rows above the health digits, which sit at the panel row itself. The panel row is read from workspace_template, whose copy in page &0D, made by reset_workspace, is hero_panel_y.

on_entry.Y: row within the hero's panel section

subroutines.name: lose_health_point
subroutines.title: Take one health point from a hero
subroutines.description:
If hero X is in play, take one point from their health and redraw it in the status panel; if that point was their last, kill them.

Every kind of harm is paid through here, one call per point: a hero walking into a monster (move_heroes, 1 point), a monster stepping onto a hero (hero_damage_taken points), a missile (its damage), an energy drainer (10, from collect_objects) and the cost of magic (6 for the Ranger, 3 for the Magic-User). Three callers use it only to draw a health they have set one point high: draw_status_panel (99 + 1 at each level), the potion, and a returning hero (33, drawn as 32).

Health is two digit sprites, hero_health_tens and hero_health_units (&1E-&27 for 0-9), so the units digit wraps from 0 to 9 with a borrow from the tens. Health 00 is still alive; the hero dies when a point is taken from 00, which leaves the tens at &1D, one below the 0 sprite: the play loop tests that to count the dead. On death the hero's sprite is erased from every view, they leave play (direction 0), the death animation is started (frame step +1, counter 1, run by move_heroes) and their number + 1 is put in the first free entry of returning_hero_queue, for a Cross of Resurrection to bring back. The health is not redrawn on death. A hero out of play (dying, returning, or not playing) loses nothing, so a skull is safe to touch.

subroutines.name: add_point
subroutines.title: Add one point to a hero's score
subroutines.description:
Add one to hero X's score and redraw it in the status panel. Points come one at a time from here: a monster killed by a missile or by magic, a hit on an energy drainer, food (five calls) and a door opened (seven); draw_status_panel calls it at each level just to draw the score, which adds a point. Bigger rewards go through add_ten_points.

The score is kept as digit sprites, one table per digit (hero_score_thousands, _hundreds, _tens, _units; &1E-&27 for 0-9), so it can be plotted as it stands. A units digit past 9 is set back to 0 and the carry made by falling into add_ten_points, which goes on into the hundreds and, through add_thousand_points, the thousands and the small ten-thousands digit. draw_score then plots all four main digits.

subroutines.name: add_ten_points
subroutines.title: Add ten points to a hero's score
subroutines.description: Add ten to hero X's score, carrying into the hundreds and through add_thousand_points, and redraw the score. collect_objects calls it for treasure (twice: 20 points), the Cross of Resurrection and every magic item; add_point falls into it to carry from the units. The units digit is not touched, which the potion relies on: it reads the units digit before calling this.

subroutines.name: point_at_boots_icon
subroutines.title: Set the position of a hero's boots icon
subroutines.description: Set plot_x to the panel's column &4A and plot_y to eight pixel rows above hero X's panel row (hero_panel_y), where the lightning bolt shows that the hero wears Boots of Speed. collect_objects calls it before plot_boots_icon, when boots are picked up, and before erase_boots_icon, when any object is found under the hero.

subroutines.name: plot_boots_icon
subroutines.title: Show a hero's boots icon
subroutines.description: Plot the lightning bolt at plot_x, plot_y, where point_at_boots_icon has just pointed, to show that hero X now wears Boots of Speed. Called when the boots are picked up. The plot goes through plot_keeping_x, which keeps the hero number across plot_sprite (which leaves X = 0).

subroutines.name: erase_boots_icon
subroutines.title: Remove a hero's boots icon
subroutines.description: Plot the blank boots sprite over the lightning bolt at plot_x, plot_y, where point_at_boots_icon has just pointed. collect_objects calls this whenever a hero finds any object, since every find takes the boots off. Falls into plot_keeping_x.

subroutines.name: hero_menu
subroutines.title: Choose the heroes and the sound
subroutines.description:
The screen before each game where the players choose who plays. It is called once per game, when a new game starts, after reset_hero has given every hero their starting attributes and before the first level. Set a text window the full width of the screen (MODE 2's 20 columns) and clear it, print the menu (print_menu) and read keys until SPACE. Keys 1-4 toggle a hero between YES and NO by flipping their hero_absent flag and rewriting the menu entry; 5 and 6 switch the sound on and off with OSBYTE &D2. After each change the whole menu is reprinted. SPACE returns, so the game starts, only if at least one hero is playing. Before each key is read, the keyboard buffer is flushed and CAPS LOCK is forced on with SHIFT LOCK off. 

Neither hero_absent nor the menu text is set up here: the menu opens with whatever they held, which after a game over in the same load is the last game's choices. The ON/OFF entry shows only what was last chosen on the menu, not the sound suppression actually in force. hero_absent is read by remove_absent_heroes at each level.

subroutines.name: remove_absent_heroes
subroutines.title: Take the heroes nobody plays out of the level
subroutines.description:
The last step of setting up each level, called by level_loop after draw_status_panel and just before play_level. For each hero in turn: 

First redraw the small ten-thousands line under the score, if it has one (through draw_ten_thousands), since start_level cleared the screen and draw_status_panel draws only the four large digits. 

Then, if the hero was switched off on the menu (hero_absent), take them out of play, since reset_workspace has just given every hero their starting state: direction 0; step_out_of_play, so move_heroes passes over them; frame 8 and dead health, so that play_level treats them as dead with their death animation over, and level_loop counts them among the dead (and resets them) when the level ends; map x &1F; and a nobody_returns entry in returning_hero_queue, which reset_monsters has just emptied. The absent heroes' entries go at the front of the queue, in hero order; a Cross of Resurrection sends such an entry to the back and takes the next. Their panel section keeps the health and score just drawn.

subroutines.name: reset_workspace
subroutines.title: Reset the game workspace for a new level
subroutines.description: Put the heroes, missiles and views back where every level starts. Called by start_level once a level, after unpack_level and before reset_monsters. Copy the 256 bytes of workspace_template (&7D00) over page &0D, the per-level workspace, then reset the exit animation's state, which lives in page &09: no hero going down the exit (exit_busy 0) or left shrunk (shrunk_hero &FF), the shrinking hero's pixel offsets (x 1, 1, 0, 0 and y 5, 3, 1, 0 for exit_shrinks_left 1-4), and trapdoor 0 as the next one a monster comes out of (next_trapdoor). Nothing here touches the heroes' health or scores, which carry over from level to level.

subroutines.name: draw_view_frames
subroutines.title: Draw the frames round the four views
subroutines.description: Draw the play screen's four view frames and the room in each view. Called last by start_level, with (plot_x) at view_frame_plots. WRCHV is first pointed back at the MOS's own routine (saved_wrchv), because wrch_handler swaps the code of any letter or digit for character 128, which would corrupt any PLOT coordinate byte that happens to be one. Then send the twenty five-byte commands as VDU 25s, call draw_all_views to draw the room each hero's view shows, and point WRCHV at wrch_handler again, so text that follows is in the game's font.

subroutines.name: unpack_level
subroutines.title: Copy the loaded level into the game's tables
subroutines.description: Bring the level just loaded into play. Called by start_level once the level file at &6B00 has been decrypted and checked, before reset_workspace. Copy objects 1-30 (position and type; the type is also the sprite), doors 1-20 (position and sprite), keys 1-20, trapdoors 0-7, &C9 bytes each of the wall map (into room_walls, read by test_wall) and object-free map (into object_free_map, read by test_object_free), and the level's 4 x 12 wall block into wall_sprite, sprite 0, the wall in every room. Entry 0 of the object, door and key tables is not touched. room_walls is also character 128's definition, which the game's text output overwrites, so this must follow the printing of the level number. The file itself lies in screen rows 23-24 and is wiped by start_level's clear_text_area once unpacked.

subroutines.name: reset_monsters
subroutines.title: Clear the monsters for a new level
subroutines.description: Start every monster dead and every hero empty-handed. Called by start_level after reset_workspace. Give monsters 1-30 the blank sprite (the first stage of dying) and an x off the map, so update_monsters brings each out of a trapdoor in turn, with monster_start_hit_points, the hit points level_loop set for this level. Then, for each of the four heroes, clear their returning_hero_queue entry, the key they carry (hero_key) and the swap flag (hero_key_dropped), and the cell kept for the door and Chalice checks (hero_door_x, hero_door_y), so nothing from the last level opens a door or wins the game. remove_absent_heroes refills the queue later for heroes nobody plays.

subroutines.name: clear_text_area
subroutines.title: Clear the screen
subroutines.description: Clear the screen above the game code. Called twice for each level: by the routine start_level calls first, before the level is loaded, and by start_level itself before the play screen is drawn. Set a text window the full 20 columns wide from row 0 to the bottom row (24 in play), and clear it with VDU 12. The window never reaches below row 24 because MODE 2's rows 25-31, &6E80-&7FFF, hold game code. The window is left set, so later text and clears stay inside it.

subroutines.name: check_for_victory
subroutines.title: Check whether the Chalice has been found
subroutines.description:
End the game in victory when a hero reaches the Chalice. Called by play_level first in every frame, before update_game. On levels other than 25 return at once. On level 25, test each hero's hero_door_x, hero_door_y, the cell move_heroes recorded as the one they last stepped or tried to step into (kept even when a wall stops them, so walking into the Chalice is enough). If it is one of the Chalice's four cells, x &1A-&1B and y 4-5, the game is won: play victory_sequence, set a text window over the views (columns 0-16, rows 0-24, leaving the status panel), clear it, print the ending text, flush the keyboard buffer, wait for a key and call the MOS's reset code through the RESET vector, so this never returns.

The ending text is not part of the program: it is the 140 bytes at room_walls + &3A followed by the zero-terminated string at object_free_map + &3A, which on level 25 hold text instead of map data. Both lie clear of &0C00-&0C07, the definition of character 128 that wrch_handler rewrites for every letter or digit it prints. The Chalice's cells are fixed here, not read from the level's objects.

subroutines.name: victory_sequence
subroutines.title: Play the victory sequence
subroutines.description:
Sparkles circle the Chalice to a rising, quickening bell tone, and the Chalice dissolves into black. Called by check_for_victory once a hero reaches the Chalice; play is frozen meanwhile, as nothing else runs.

Each pass sounds the bell, draws the ring of sparkles round the Chalice (draw_victory_ring), and waits. The bell's pitch climbs by a step each pass and wraps past 255, and each time it wraps the step grows by 1, so the tone repeats as ever faster sweeps: about 256 x (1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/50), some 1,150 passes in all. The wait starts at &E6 units of about 1,280 cycles each and shortens by one a pass down to 1, reached on pass 229, near the end of the first sweep; from then on each pass also calls dissolve_chalice, which clears a random byte of the Chalice when its random value is below &C0. After the 50th wrap (erase_victory_ring), erase the ring, clear whatever is left of the Chalice's sprite, replot it black, and wait 255 vertical syncs, about five seconds. The Chalice's sprite data stays cleared, as the game resets next.

OSBYTEs &D4 and &D5 set (old AND Y) EOR X, and Y is never set for them: the bell's envelope byte takes Y left over from the frame, and the first pitch takes the Y that OSBYTE &D4 returns; later passes have Y = 0 from the wait loop, so the pitch is exactly victory_pitch.

subroutines.name: draw_victory_ring
subroutines.title: Draw the ring of sprites round the Chalice
subroutines.description: Draw one frame of the sparkling ring. Called by victory_sequence once a pass, and once more with the blank sprite to erase the ring. Plot victory_sprite at the twelve cells round the Chalice's 2 x 2 block (x &19-&1C, y 3-6, all in the Chalice's room), from x &1C, y 3 leftwards along the top, down the left side, along the bottom and up the right side, three cells to a side, each corner starting a side. The sprite moves on to the next sparkle (next_victory_sprite) after each of the first three sides and is left at the fourth side's, so the next ring starts with it and the sparkles move one side round the ring each pass. With the blank sprite, it erases the ring.

on_entry.victory_sprite: the sprite for the top side

on_exit.victory_sprite: the sprite of the right side

subroutines.name: plot_victory_sprite
subroutines.title: Plot a victory sprite at a cell
subroutines.description: Plot victory_sprite at the cell ring_x, ring_y in every view showing it, with the pixel offsets victory_sequence cleared. Called by draw_victory_ring for each of the ring's twelve cells; ring_x and ring_y are left as they were, for the next step.

subroutines.name: next_victory_sprite
subroutines.title: Choose the next victory sprite
subroutines.description: Step victory_sprite through the four sparkles, &16-&19, wrapping back to &16. Called by draw_victory_ring between the ring's sides, so each side shows a different sparkle. The blank sprite, &15, used to erase the ring, is left alone, so an erasing ring stays blank all the way round.

on_exit.victory_sprite: the next sparkle, &16-&19 in turn; &15 (erasing) is kept

subroutines.name: dissolve_chalice
subroutines.title: Clear a random byte of the Chalice
subroutines.description: Eat one more hole in the Chalice. Called by victory_sequence on every pass once its wait is down to 1. Make a random number from the System VIA's timer 1 low byte mixed with two bytes of MOS workspace (&FC and &FA). If it is below &C0, the size of the Chalice's 8 x 24-byte sprite, zero that byte of sprite_chalice and replot the Chalice, so it dissolves into black a pixel pair at a time; otherwise do nothing this pass. A byte already clear may be chosen again, so some survive until erase_victory_ring clears the rest.

subroutines.name: plot_chalice
subroutines.title: Plot the Chalice
subroutines.description: Plot sprite &73, the Chalice, at its top-left cell (x &1A, y 4) in every view showing it, as its sprite data now stands. Called by dissolve_chalice after each byte it clears, and at the end of victory_sequence to show it gone. The sprite is two cells wide and two high, so it covers the four cells check_for_victory tests. The pixel offsets are those victory_sequence cleared.

subroutines.name: update_game
subroutines.title: Run one frame of play
subroutines.description:
Do all of a frame's play apart from the exit. Called by play_level once a frame, after check_for_victory; play_level deals with the exit when this returns. The work, in order:

1. move_heroes: each hero in play walks, fires or casts magic, is redrawn, and picks up any object in their cell. It records in hero_door_x/y the cell each hero stepped or tried to step into.

2. Doors (check_doors): for each hero in turn, doors 20 to 1 are compared with that cell. If one is there and the hero carries its key (key n opens door n; hero_key 0 means none, and there is no door 0), the door opens: the hero scores 7 points, the door sound plays (food_sound at a lower pitch), the door is erased from every view, its wall bit in room_walls is cleared, its entry in door_x/door_y is moved off the map, and the key is used up and its panel icon erased. At most one door opens per hero per frame. Every hero is tested, in play or not.

3. Keys (draw_keys): every key on the floor is redrawn, then each hero is checked. A dead hero whose death animation has finished drops their key where they fell. A hero in play, or still dying, who stands on a key picks it up and leaves the key they carried, if any, in its place; hero_key_dropped makes them skip the next frame, so one who stays on the cell swaps back on the frame after.

4. draw_objects: the objects are replotted, repairing any cell a moving sprite has crossed.

5. move_missiles: each missile in flight moves one cell and hits what it meets.

6. update_monsters: the trapdoors are redrawn and the monsters move.

7. The pause key: if it is held, the game freezes here until it is pressed again. OSBYTE &7A reports only the lowest-numbered key held, so a held movement key can hide it.

subroutines.name: hero_enters_exit
subroutines.title: Start a hero going down the exit
subroutines.description:
Start hero X's descent: the hero spins on the exit for four turns, shrinking after each of the first three. Called by play_level's check_exit for a hero who has just stepped onto the exit, after drop_key, and after the hero has been taken out of play and the exit hidden off the map.

queue_exit_marker plays the exit sound and puts a nobody_returns marker in returning_hero_queue, as remove_absent_heroes does for a hero nobody plays. Any hero shrunk on an earlier descent (shrunk_hero) gets their full-size sprites back, as the sprites are shared with no copy. Then exit_busy is set, exiting_hero and shrunk_hero become X, exit_spin starts at -1 (the first frame's +2 gives the up-facing sprite) and exit_shrinks_left at 4; play_level's redraw_exit runs the spin from the next frame.

It ends by jumping to play_level rather than returning, so its return address (into check_exit at &1F8E) stays on the stack until the level ends; see play_level.

subroutines.name: restore_hero_sprites
subroutines.title: Restore a hero's sprite sizes
subroutines.description: Give hero X back their full-size sprites after the exit animation has shrunk them. The descent narrows sprites base + 1 to base + 7 (base from hero_sprites) by a byte and shortens them by three rows after each of three turns, in sprite_widths and sprite_heights themselves. This sets the seven back to a whole cell, 4 bytes wide and 12 rows high, which is what every hero's walking sprites measure. Called by hero_enters_exit, before the next hero's descent shrinks their own sprites, and by play_level when the level ends, each time for shrunk_hero.

subroutines.name: drop_key
subroutines.title: Drop the key a hero carries
subroutines.description:
Leave hero X's key behind beside the exit, so the heroes still playing can use it. Called by play_level's check_exit as the hero steps onto the exit, before they are taken out of play.

find_open_neighbour picks the first wall-free cell of those above, right of and below the hero, or else the cell to the left whatever it holds; another key or an object may already lie there. The key's key_x/key_y are set to that cell, so update_game's draw_keys shows it from the next frame; hero_key is cleared and the key icon erased from the hero's panel section. A hero with no key moves key entry 0, which is never drawn or picked up.

subroutines.name: find_open_neighbour
subroutines.title: Find a free cell next to a cell
subroutines.description: Find where drop_key, its only caller, can put down a key next to the exit. Starting from cell_x, cell_y, try the cells above, to the right and below, in that order, through test_wall, and leave cell_x, cell_y on the first without a wall; failing all three, leave them on the cell to the left without testing it, so a key can land in a wall there. Only walls are tested, not keys, objects or creatures. map_ptr is left pointing at the room of the last cell tested.

on_exit.cell_x: x of the first free neighbour, trying above, right and below; otherwise the cell to the left, unchecked
on_exit.Y: 0 if a free neighbour was found

subroutines.name: queue_exit_marker
subroutines.title: Sound the exit and add a queue marker
subroutines.description: Play the exit's falling tone and queue a marker for the hero leaving. Called first by hero_enters_exit, when a hero steps onto the exit. Define envelope 3 from exit_envelope and play exit_sound with it (channel 2, pitch 250). Then put a &64 (nobody_returns) entry in the first empty (zero) entry of returning_hero_queue, behind any dead heroes waiting, as remove_absent_heroes does for each hero nobody plays. A Cross of Resurrection passes such markers to the back of the queue, so a hero who took the exit is never brought back by one. At most four of the queue's five entries are ever in use, so an empty one is always found; X is not bounded.

subroutines.name: move_heroes
subroutines.title: Move the heroes
subroutines.description:
Let each of the four heroes, in turn from the Ranger, walk, fire or cast magic for this frame, redraw them, and let them pick up what lies in their cell. update_game calls this first in every frame, before the door and key tests (which use the cells it records in hero_door_x/y), draw_objects, move_missiles and update_monsters.

A hero out of play is passed over if nobody plays them (step &63), or handed to animate_absent_hero if dying or returning through a Cross. A hero half way through a step (step 1) finishes it through continue_hero_step and reads no keys. Otherwise heroes 0 and 1 first go through check_magic, which comes back to read_hero_keys, or after a cast to draw_moved_hero with no move; then the first held of up, down, right, left and fire decides. A direction turns the hero that way (directions 1, 3, 5, 7) and tries the next cell, which is recorded in hero_door_x/y whatever is there, so a hero pushing on a door opens it. A wall or closed door, a monster (alive or dying, found by find_creature) or another hero in play refuses the move; walking into a monster also costs one health point, whatever the hero's armour. A move into another room is made at once and switches the hero's view (show_hero_room); within a room the Boots of Speed make it at once too, and without them the hero stays in the old cell, drawn half a cell along, and arrives on the next frame. Fire puts a missile in the first of the hero's free slots (3 x hero up to hero_max_missiles of them), in the hero's own cell, with bit 7 of its direction set so move_missiles does not erase it off the hero; the bell (VDU 7) sounds and the hero's frame flips. With no slot free, or no key held, the hero stands still.

A hero who moved or was refused is erased from where they were drawn, using previous_x/y and previous_offset_x/y; every hero still in play is then drawn, and collect_objects runs whenever object_free_map lets their cell hold an object, every frame they are there and not only on arrival. check_magic's delay returns from move_heroes itself, so after a cast the later heroes are not moved for three frames. The bytes at &6F6D are never executed.

subroutines.name: start_hero_step
subroutines.title: Start a hero's step between cells
subroutines.description: Called by move_heroes when a direction key starts a move within a room and the hero has no Boots of Speed. Set hero X's step counter to 1 and their pixel offsets to half a cell in the direction they face (hero_direction 1, 3, 5 or 7: up, right, down, left): 6 rows up or down, or 2 byte columns left or right. move_heroes then draws the hero there, half way to the next cell, for one frame, still recorded in the old cell; continue_hero_step completes the move on the next frame.

subroutines.name: continue_hero_step
subroutines.title: Continue a hero's step between cells
subroutines.description: Called by move_heroes, in place of reading the hero's keys, on the frame after a step starts. Toggle hero X's walking frame and count down their step. When it ends, move the hero one cell in the direction they face and clear the pixel offsets, so a step takes two frames. The offsets are then doubled. Since start_hero_step sets the counter to 1 and nothing else gives an in-play hero a non-zero step, the step always ends here, so the doubling only ever doubles zero offsets.

subroutines.name: animate_absent_hero
subroutines.title: Animate a hero who is out of play
subroutines.description:
Play a dying hero's sparkles and skull, or a returning hero's skull and sparkles in reverse, at the cell where they fell. move_heroes calls this each frame, in the hero's turn, for a hero out of play (direction 0) unless nobody plays them (step &63). While out of play the hero's offset bytes are reused: hero_offset_y is a two-frame timer and hero_offset_x the step through the sequence (+1 or -1), both set by lose_health_point for a death and by collect_objects for a Cross of Resurrection.

Every other frame, plot hero_appearance_sprites entry hero_frame at the hero's cell, with no pixel offset, then step hero_frame by hero_offset_x: forwards (+1) for a hero dying, stopping at the skull (entry 8), which is then redrawn every other frame until a Cross brings the hero back; backwards (-1) for a hero returning through a Cross of Resurrection, from entry 8. A dying hero starts from their walking frame (0 or 1), which lose_health_point does not reset, so the first sparkle may be skipped. A returning hero is put back in play as hero_frame reaches 0, so entry 0 is never shown on the way back: they come back in the cell where they fell, facing down, standing squarely in it, with health 32 (set to 33 and drawn by taking a point). move_heroes draws them on their next turn.

subroutines.name: draw_hero
subroutines.title: Draw a hero
subroutines.description: Plot sprite_number at hero X's cell, shifted by their pixel offsets (half a cell along while a step is under way), in every view that shows it. move_heroes calls it each frame for every hero in play, at draw_moved_hero, with the hero's sprite for their direction and frame; lose_health_point calls it with the blank to erase a hero who has just died. cell_x and cell_y are left as plot_at_cell leaves them, as positions within the view, so callers needing the map cell load it again.

subroutines.name: get_hero_cell
subroutines.title: Copy a hero's position to cell_x, cell_y
subroutines.description: Load hero X's map cell into cell_x and cell_y, ready for plot_at_cell. Used by draw_hero and animate_absent_hero.

subroutines.name: draw_objects
subroutines.title: Draw the level's objects
subroutines.description:
Draw every object still on the level (treasure, food, teleporters, drainers, magic items, the exit) in whichever views show it. update_game calls this every frame, after move_heroes and the door and key checks and before move_missiles and update_monsters, so an object that a hero has just walked off or a monster has crossed is put back before the next sprites are drawn over it.

Objects 30 (the exit) down to 1 are plotted with plot_at_cell, their type being their sprite, squarely in their cells (no pixel offset). Object 0 is not drawn. A collected or worn-away object has map x and y &FF (off_map), which plot_at_cell works out to a room offset (&DB) that no view shows, so it is not drawn.

subroutines.name: collect_objects
subroutines.title: Pick up the object in a hero's cell
subroutines.description:
Give hero X whatever lies in the cell they have just stepped into: pick up treasure, food, the Cross or a magic item, ride a teleporter, or suffer an energy drainer. move_heroes calls this every frame for each hero in play, after drawing them (draw_moved_hero), whether they moved, stood still or fired, and only when object_free_map says the hero's cell can hold an object. A pickup is removed at once, so it acts once; a drainer stays and acts on every frame the hero's cell is its cell: the frame of arrival, each frame standing on it, and the half-step frame of leaving it (the hero's cell changes only on arrival), so walking across one within a room costs at least 20 health.

Objects 30 down to 1 are compared with the hero's cell and the first match is acted on. Finding any object at all takes off the hero's Boots of Speed and erases the bolt from the panel, before the type is looked at, so the boots are lost to a teleporter, a drainer or the exit as well as to a pickup. Then, by type (object_type, which is also the sprite):

&28 treasure: 20 points and the treasure sound; removed.

&29 food: 10 health (to at most 99), 5 points and the food sound; removed.

&2B teleporter: the hero is moved to the cell above the previous teleporter in the object list, searching back and wrapping from object 0 to 29, so each leads to the one before it and the first to the last; the cell is not tested for walls or creatures, and a lone teleporter leads to itself. The teleport sound plays and show_hero_room redraws the view. The teleporter stays.

&2A Cross of Resurrection: 10 points and the pickup sound; removed, and the first hero in returning_hero_queue starts to materialise where they fell. With nobody waiting it is wasted.

&51 the exit: passed over (update_game's check_hero_on_exit deals with it) and the search goes on.

&5F and up, magic items: removed, the pickup sound and 10 points, then &5F Boots of Speed (bolt icon, a whole cell per step), &60 helmet (one less health lost per monster blow, to at least 3, and the armour rating redrawn), &61 potion (health set to the score's units digit twice over, e.g. 77), &62 pile of weapons (one more missile in flight, to at most 3, and its icon) and anything else, &63, the magic sword (one more missile damage, to at most 9, redrawn).

Anything else (&53-&5E, an energy drainer at one of its stages): hit_sound at pitch &32 and 10 health lost, one point at a time, which can kill. The drainer stays.

Treasure, food, the Cross and magic items are removed by setting their map x and y to &FF (off_map), so they are neither drawn nor found again.

subroutines.name: play_pickup_sound
subroutines.title: Play the pickup sound
subroutines.description: Play the sound of a Cross or magic item being picked up. collect_objects calls it for both. Envelope 3 is defined as the pickup envelope and the pickup sound played with it on the noise channel, from the OSWORD parameter blocks pickup_envelope and pickup_sound. Envelope 3 is shared with the treasure, key and exit sounds, which define their own, so it is defined again each time.

subroutines.name: move_missiles
subroutines.title: Move the missiles
subroutines.description:
Fly every missile in flight one cell and settle what it hits. update_game calls this each frame, after move_heroes (which fires them) and draw_objects, and before update_monsters, which plays out the deaths it causes.

Each of the twelve slots (three per hero, from 3 x hero) with a non-zero missile_direction is in flight. It is erased from its cell, unless fired this frame (bit 7 set) and so still on its hero, whose frame flip_firer_frame then flips back. It moves one cell in its direction (1-4: up, right, down, left), a cell a frame with no pixel offset, and the new cell is tried in turn, with the slot kept on the stack throughout. A wall spends the missile. A live monster takes its damage through monster_hit, which spends the missile and, for a kill, gives the firer a point; a monster already sparkling lets it through. The test for live is a sprite below the first sparkle, so a monster killed earlier in the frame (sprite blank until update_monsters runs) can be hit again. An energy drainer is worn down a stage, and removed after its last; the firer scores a point and the missile is turned round in the drainer's cell, so it can fly back into its firer. Any hero in the cell, the firer included and whether in play or not (a skull stops it), spends the missile, and lose_health_point takes missile_damage points, one at a time, from a hero in play. Otherwise the missile is drawn in its new cell as missile_sprite_base + direction, the weapon pointing the way it flies. A spent missile is not drawn, and its direction 0 frees the slot for its hero's next shot. Missiles pass through one another and through objects other than drainers.

subroutines.name: flip_firer_frame
subroutines.title: Animate the hero who fired a missile
subroutines.description: Toggle the animation frame (0 or 1) of the hero whose missile is in slot X, so the hero's sprite changes as they throw. move_missiles calls this on a missile's first move, while bit 7 of its direction still marks it as just fired; move_heroes flipped the frame when it fired, so this flips it back, and the throw shows for one frame. The firer is told by the missile's sprite base (one less than its up sprite): arrows the Ranger, fireballs the Magic-User, axes the Barbarian, and anything else the Fighter. The hero is not redrawn here; the new frame shows when move_heroes next draws them.

subroutines.name: credit_missile_owner
subroutines.title: Give a point to the hero who fired a missile
subroutines.description: Score one point for the hero whose missile is in slot X. move_missiles calls this when a missile kills a monster (through monster_killed) and when it wears down an energy drainer. The firer is told by the missile's sprite base, as in flip_firer_frame: arrows the Ranger, fireballs the Magic-User, axes the Barbarian, and anything else the Fighter. add_point adds the point and redraws the score, whether or not the firer is still in play.

subroutines.name: draw_all_views
subroutines.title: Draw all four views
subroutines.description: Draw the walls and doors of the room in each hero's view: the Ranger's top left, the Magic-User's top right, the Barbarian's bottom left and the Fighter's bottom right. draw_view_frames calls it once as each level starts, after drawing the frames round the views, when every view_room entry holds the heroes' starting room. A view is drawn even for a hero nobody plays. Since each draw_room plots every door in every view showing its room, the doors of a room shared by several views are drawn several times over. Heroes, monsters and objects appear as the first frame of play plots them.

subroutines.name: show_hero_room
subroutines.title: Show the room a hero has moved into
subroutines.description:
Make hero X's view show the room they are now in, and redraw that view's walls and doors. move_heroes calls this when a hero steps into another room, and a teleporter jumps here after moving the hero.

Each hero has a fixed view (0 top left to 3 bottom right). test_wall is called on the hero's cell only for the room offset it leaves in map_ptr; that becomes the low byte of the view's view_room entry (view_room + 2 x hero), the pointer into room_walls that draw_view_0 to draw_view_3 and plot_at_cell read; the high byte never changes. The matching draw_view_n then draws the room's walls and doors. Creatures and objects appear in the new view as they are next plotted.

subroutines.name: draw_view_0
subroutines.title: Draw the top-left view
subroutines.description: Draw the walls and doors of the room in hero 0's view, the Ranger's, whose top-left cell starts at byte column 1, pixel row 1 (see plot_at_cell for the view coordinates). draw_all_views calls this as a level starts, and show_hero_room when hero 0 enters another room. The view's corner is passed to draw_room in plot_y and, for want of a spare variable, in cell_x; only the low byte of view_room is passed, in map_ptr, as draw_room supplies page &0C.

subroutines.name: draw_view_1
subroutines.title: Draw the top-right view
subroutines.description: Draw the room in hero 1's view, the Magic-User's, whose top-left is byte column &23, pixel row 1. Called as draw_view_0 is.

subroutines.name: draw_view_2
subroutines.title: Draw the bottom-left view
subroutines.description: Draw the room in hero 2's view, the Barbarian's, whose top-left is byte column 1, pixel row &67. Called as draw_view_0 is.

subroutines.name: draw_view_3
subroutines.title: Draw the bottom-right view
subroutines.description: Draw the room in hero 3's view, the Fighter's, whose top-left is byte column &23, pixel row &67. Called as draw_view_0 is.

subroutines.name: draw_room
subroutines.title: Draw a room
subroutines.description:
Repaint one view with the walls of its room and the level's doors, wiping whatever the view showed before. Called by draw_view_0 to draw_view_3, so as a level starts and whenever a hero changes room.

The room's eight wall bytes (see test_wall for the map layout) are read through map_ptr, whose high byte is set here to page &0C (room_walls). Each byte is one row of cells: draw_room_row plots a wall block or a blank in each of its eight cells, and plot_y moves down twelve pixel rows for the next. Every cell is painted, so this also wipes the previous room's creatures and objects; they reappear as they are next plotted. Then each of doors 20 to 1 is plotted at its map cell through plot_at_cell, which draws it only in views whose room holds it, and in every such view, not just this one. A closed door's cell is also a wall in room_walls, so it is first drawn as a wall block and then covered by the door; an opened door has its wall bit cleared and its position set to off_map, so it is drawn nowhere.

on_entry.map_ptr: the room's offset in room_walls (the low byte)

subroutines.name: draw_room_row
subroutines.title: Draw one row of a room
subroutines.description: Plot a wall block or a blank in each of the eight cells of one row of a view, from bit 7 of scratch (the leftmost cell) to bit 0, four byte columns apart, starting at byte column cell_x. Called by draw_room for each row. The cells are plotted with plot_sprite directly, in this view only.

on_entry.scratch: the row's eight wall bits, the leftmost cell in bit 7

on_exit.plot_x: cell_x + 32, just right of the view

subroutines.name: plot_at_cell
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite at a map cell in every view
subroutines.description:
Draw (or, with the blank sprite, erase) sprite_number at a map cell, in every view that is showing the cell's room. Heroes, skulls, monsters, sparkles, missiles, objects, keys, doors, trapdoors and the Chalice are all drawn and erased through here; only the walls (draw_room_row) and the status panel are plotted directly. So a cell in a room that two heroes share is drawn in both views, and one in a room that no view shows is not drawn at all.

Map coordinates. The dungeon is a grid of cells, x across from 0 at the left, y down from 0 at the top, divided into rooms of 8x8 cells, four rooms across (x 0-31) and six down (y 0-47). A room is named by its offset in room_walls, 32 x its row of rooms + 8 x its column of rooms, which is (y AND &F8) x 4 + (x AND &F8): always a multiple of 8, from 0 to &B8 (test_wall describes the map's bytes). The cell's place within its room is x AND 7, y AND 7.

View coordinates. plot_sprite takes a byte column (plot_x, 0-79 across the screen, two MODE 2 pixels each) and a pixel row (plot_y, from 0 at the top). Each view shows one room, 8 cells of 4 byte columns by 8 cells of 12 pixel rows (32 x 96), with its top-left at column 1 or view_right_column (&23) and row 1 or view_bottom_row (&67): hero 0's view top left, 1 top right, 2 bottom left, 3 bottom right. view_room + 2 x hero holds the offset of the room each view shows. A cell's sprite goes at the view's corner + ((x AND 7) x 4 + plot_offset_x, (y AND 7) x 12 + plot_offset_y). The offsets are signed (&FA is 6 rows up) and place a sprite part way between cells while it steps.

The room offset is worked out once and compared with the low byte of each view_room entry, views 0 to 3 in turn. A cell at off_map (&FF, &FF), where collected objects, opened doors and parked monsters are put, comes out as &DB, through the carries of the sum: not a multiple of 8, so no view shows it and it is never drawn. There is no clipping, but no hero's or monster's step crosses a room edge, so a stepping sprite stays inside its view.

cell_x and cell_y are overwritten with the position within the room, so a caller that needs the map cell again sets them again; code that reads them afterwards without doing so sees these view positions.

on_exit.cell_room: the cell's room, as an offset into room_walls

subroutines.name: test_wall
subroutines.title: Test for a wall at a map cell
subroutines.description:
Say whether a map cell is solid: a wall, or a door not yet opened. Heroes (move_heroes), missiles (move_missiles) and monsters (update_monsters) test here the cell they are about to enter, and find_open_neighbour the cells next to the exit where drop_key can put a key down. check_magic and show_hero_room call it only for the room pointer it leaves in map_ptr.

The wall map. room_walls (&0C00) holds eight bytes per room, one per row of cells from the top, and one bit per cell, bit 7 for the leftmost (x AND 7 = 0) to bit 0 for the rightmost; a set bit is solid. Rooms are stored in rows of four, left to right, so a room's eight bytes start at (y AND &F8) x 4 + (x AND &F8) (see plot_at_cell for the coordinates), and the cell is bit bit_masks[x AND 7] of byte y AND 7 there. object_free_map at &2100 has the same layout (test_object_free). The level file supplies both; opening a door clears its bit.

The bit is returned in A and Y, with Z set for an open cell; callers that have pulled X from the stack test Y. map_ptr is left pointing at the room's bytes, its low byte being the room offset that view_room uses. Coordinates off the map are not checked: off_map (&FF, &FF) reads a byte beyond the wall map. The bit is also stored in &8F (victory_pitch), which the victory sequence sets before it reads it, so the copy is never used.

subroutines.name: test_object_free
subroutines.title: Test whether a map cell can hold an object
subroutines.description:
Say whether an object might lie in a map cell, so that the object list need be searched only there. move_heroes calls it for a hero who has moved, before collect_objects, and move_missiles for a missile's new cell, before looking for an energy drainer.

The same calculation as test_wall, on object_free_map at &2100 instead of room_walls: eight bytes per room, a bit per cell, bit 7 at the left. A clear bit means an object may lie there; the map comes from the level file and is not changed when an object is collected, so a cleared cell goes on costing a search that finds nothing. The bit is returned in A and Y, with Z set if an object may lie there, and also stored in &8F (victory_pitch), where nothing reads it. map_ptr is left pointing into object_free_map.

on_exit.Z: set if an object may lie there

subroutines.name: find_creature
subroutines.title: Look for a monster or hero at a cell
subroutines.description:
Say whether a creature stands in a map cell, and if a monster has walked into a hero, hurt the hero. Called by move_heroes and move_missiles for the cell a hero or missile is entering, and by update_monsters for the cell a monster steps into and for the trapdoor a dead monster comes back at (monster_reappears).

Monsters 30 to 1 are compared first, skipping monster number scratch; the first whose cell matches is returned. If none matches and scratch is non-zero (a monster is asking), heroes 0 to 3 are compared too, and the first one found loses hero_damage_taken points of health, one at a time through lose_health_point. A hero or missile passes scratch = 0, so only monsters are looked for (they test heroes their own way); a monster passes its own number, so it skips itself and is blocked by, and hurts, a hero in its way, every frame it tries.

Neither search looks at state: a dying monster still fills its cell, and a hero out of play (a skull) blocks a monster too, though lose_health_point takes nothing from them. A found monster is reported with A = Y = cell_y, so one in map row 0 would read as nothing found. monster_reappears calls this without loading the trapdoor's cell, so it tests the view position plot_at_cell left in cell_x, cell_y; a hero who happens to stand at that cell is hurt.

on_exit.A: cell_y if a monster was found, 1 if a hero, else 0
on_exit.Y: cell_y if a monster was found, else 0
on_exit.Z: clear if a creature was found (cell_y non-zero)
on_exit.X: the monster or hero found; else 0, or 4 after the hero search

subroutines.name: update_monsters
subroutines.title: Draw the trapdoors and move the monsters
subroutines.description:
Move every monster on by one frame of its life, and redraw the trapdoors they come out of. update_game calls it once a frame, after draw_objects and move_missiles, so a monster killed by a missile or magic this frame starts its death here.

The eight trapdoors are drawn first, because erasing a creature or missile that crossed one has blanked its cell. Then each monster, 30 down to 1, is erased where it was drawn last frame and moved on according to its state.

Moving: a monster mid-step slides a quarter cell further (continue_monster_step). One that is not stepping tries the next cell the way it faces. If that cell is open and holds no creature, it starts a step: monster_x and monster_y keep the old cell while the offsets carry the sprite across, so an interior cell takes four frames (a quarter, a half, three quarters, then square in the new cell). A cell in a room's edge row or column, in the direction of travel, is entered at once, so no sprite is drawn between two rooms and a monster crosses from one room into the next in two frames.

Blocked: a wall, a closed door or a creature in the cell keeps the monster where it is. It turns a random way, each of the four equally likely, from the System VIA's timer 1, and tries that way next frame. A monster does not chase anyone: it walks straight on until blocked. find_creature takes hero_damage_taken points from a hero it finds in the cell, so a monster hurts a hero each time it tries to step into them.

Dying: a monster killed by a missile or by magic is given sprite &15 (the blank) there. Each frame here advances it through the sparkles &16-&19, drawn where it died.

Reappearing: after the last sparkle monster_reappears puts it on the next trapdoor in turn, facing up, to be drawn next frame.

reset_monsters starts every monster at the blank with x &FF, so at the start of a level all 30 sparkle off the map together and emerge on the same frame, shared out round the eight trapdoors in turn. Only the target cell is ever tested for a creature: during a slide the monster is still recorded in the cell it is leaving, and the arrival is not checked again, so two monsters, or a monster and a hero, can end a step in the same cell. The creature test made as a monster reappears looks at the wrong cell (see monster_reappears).

subroutines.name: start_monster_step
subroutines.title: Start a monster's step between cells
subroutines.description: Called by update_monsters when a monster that is not stepping tries the next cell, before that cell is tested. Set monster X's step counter to 3 and its offsets to the first quarter of a cell in the direction it faces: 3 rows up or down, or one byte column left or right. If the cell turns out to be blocked, or on a room's edge, update_monsters clears all three again; otherwise the monster is drawn this frame a quarter of the way there, and continue_monster_step takes over on the next.

subroutines.name: continue_monster_step
subroutines.title: Continue a monster's step between cells
subroutines.description: Called by update_monsters each frame while monster X's step is under way (monster_step non-zero). Toggle its walking frame, so its legs move, and count down its step. On the first two calls the offsets grow by another quarter of a cell (a byte column or three rows), to a half and then three quarters. On the third the step ends: monster_x or monster_y moves one cell on the way it faces and the offsets are cleared, so it is drawn squarely in the new cell. With the frame start_monster_step began, a monster crosses an interior cell in four frames. Nothing tests the new cell again on arrival.

subroutines.name: test_key
subroutines.title: Test whether a key is pressed
subroutines.description: Report whether one key is held down at this moment. read_hero_keys calls it for each hero's direction and fire keys, from the hero_key tables, and check_magic for the Ranger's and Magic-User's magic keys. The key is scanned with OSBYTE &81 and a negative INKEY number (Y = &FF), which returns X = Y = &FF if it is held; the caller's X, the hero number, is kept on the stack across the call.

on_entry.A: INKEY key number (negative, as a byte)

on_exit.A: 0 if the key is pressed, 1 if not
on_exit.Z: set if the key is pressed

subroutines.name: check_magic
subroutines.title: Cast a hero's magic if their key is held
subroutines.description:
Let the Ranger or the Magic-User cast magic, which kills every live monster in the room they are in. move_heroes jumps here (JMP, not JSR) for heroes 0 and 1 when they stand in a cell, before reading their other keys.

hero_magic_delay is counted down first. It normally stands at 1, so the magic key (hero_magic_key) is scanned every frame; while it is not yet zero the RTS here returns from move_heroes itself, so neither this hero nor those after it move that frame. Without the key held, play goes on to read_hero_keys. With it held, the magic sound plays, the delay is set to 4 (three frozen frames follow) and the cost is taken one health point at a time: 6 for the Ranger, 3 for the Magic-User, which can kill the caster. Then every monster whose cell lies in the room the caster's view shows, and whose sprite is below the blank (alive), is given the blank sprite, the first frame of a death that update_monsters plays out, and the caster scores a point for each, through add_point, even if the cost has just killed them. Unlike a missile's kill, the magic does not reset the monster's hit points, so a monster wounded before comes back from its trapdoor still wounded. The caster does not move that frame: play goes on at draw_moved_hero, which draws them if still in play.

subroutines.name: play_level
subroutines.title: Play a level until it ends
subroutines.description:
The game's frame loop: play the current level until it is over. Called once per level by new_game's level loop, after the level is drawn, the status panel set up and absent heroes removed; when it returns, new_game gives each dead hero their starting attributes back, ending the game if all four died.

A frame, in order:

1. Wait for os_vsync_counter, which the MOS counts down at every vertical sync, to go negative, then set it to 2. Frames start three vsyncs apart (about 17 a second), or at once if a frame's work took longer.

2. check_for_victory: on level 25, a hero at the Chalice wins the game, and it never returns.

3. update_game: heroes, doors, keys, objects, missiles, monsters and the pause key, in that order (see its banner).

4. The level-end test, skipped while a hero is going down the exit (exit_busy). The level is over when every hero is out of play (direction 0) and no dead hero's death animation is still short of frame 8; heroes who went down the exit, or whom nobody plays, count as out of play. shrunk_hero's sprites are then restored and the loop returns.

5. check_exit: the first hero found standing on the exit drops their key beside it (drop_key), is taken out of play, erased and moved off the map (hero_x &FF), and the exit itself is moved off the map, its cell kept in exit_saved_x/y, so no other hero can enter it meanwhile. hero_enters_exit then starts the descent and jumps back to the top of the loop.

6. While exit_busy is set, redraw_exit draws one step of the descent: the exit sprite on its cell, then the hero on it turned a quarter, through up, right, down and left. On the fifth frame of each turn only the exit is drawn and the hero's sprites shrink by a byte and three rows (shrink_hero_width/height), drawn from then on with exit_offsets_x/y to keep them near the cell's centre. After four turns, 20 frames in all, restore_exit puts the exit back and clears exit_busy, so another hero can use it.

How the level ends: hero_enters_exit is entered with JSR but leaves with a JMP to play_level, so each descent leaves a return address (into check_exit at &1F8E) on the stack. The RTS at the level's end therefore returns into check_exit once for each hero who left by the exit; each such return runs one more full frame before the next RTS, and only the last returns to new_game.

subroutines.name: game_entry
subroutines.title: Start the game
subroutines.description:
The game's entry point, where the release's loader jumps once the game is in memory. It prepares the two MOS services the game leans on: 

First the bell (the BEL character's channel, envelope, pitch and duration, through OSBYTEs &D3-&D6): the bell is what sounds when a hero fires, and the victory sequence raises its pitch. 

Then the text: save the MOS's WRCHV in saved_wrchv, for draw_view_frames to put back while it sends the view frames' PLOT commands, and point WRCHV at wrch_handler, so that all the game's text is printed in its own font. 

This code lives in the per-level workspace: from &0D40 its bytes are the missile tables and other workspace in page &0D, which reset_workspace overwrites from workspace_template at the start of every level, so it can run only before the first level after the game is loaded. It does not return; what follows &0D6A, starting the game, is the release's own.

subroutines.name: decrypt_level
subroutines.title: Decrypt and check the level just loaded
subroutines.description: Decrypt the level at &6B00-&6DAF in place, XORing each byte with the low byte of its own address, and sum the decrypted bytes. If the sum does not match the level's entry in level_checksums, call &D9CD, the reset entry of MOS 1.20, so a damaged or altered level file is never played. It runs once per level, as soon as the level file is in memory and before unpack_level copies it into the game's tables; it returns only if the level is intact, leaving it decrypted at &6B00. The pointer and the sum borrow the plotter's zero-page workspace (plot_x and plot_y, sprite_width), which nothing is using while a level loads.

subroutines.name: decrypt_level_joystick
subroutines.title: Decrypt and check the level just loaded
subroutines.description: Decrypt the level at &6B00-&6DAF in place, XORing each byte with the low byte of its own address, and sum the decrypted bytes. If the sum does not match the level's entry in level_checksums, call &D9CD, the reset entry of MOS 1.20, so a damaged or altered level file is never played. It runs once per level, as soon as the level file is in memory and before unpack_level copies it into the game's tables; it returns only if the level is intact, leaving it decrypted at &6B00. The pointer and the sum borrow the plotter's zero-page workspace (plot_x and plot_y, sprite_width), which nothing is using while a level loads.

subroutines.name: start_level
subroutines.title: Set up and draw a new level
subroutines.description:
Turn the next level's file into a fresh play screen. Called from the level loop (&0E57) at the start of every level; the loop then draws the status panel and plays the level.

In order: prepare the text area (the first call, which differs between releases), get the level file at &6B00 decrypted and checked, unpack it into the game's tables (unpack_level), put the heroes, missiles and views back to the start (reset_workspace), start the monsters dead and the heroes without keys (reset_monsters), then clear the screen, set the 6845 to show all 25 character rows the play screen uses, and draw the view frames and the four views (draw_view_frames). The order matters: any text printed before loading rewrites character 128's definition at &0C00, the start of room_walls, so the level is unpacked after it; and the level file lies in screen rows 23-24, so the screen is cleared only once the file is unpacked.

subroutines.name: boot_loader
subroutines.title: Load the game file and run it (not used)
subroutines.description: Build an OSFILE control block at &6B00 naming boot_filename with load address &2000, call the filing system's FILEV handler to load the file, and jump to &2000. &0740 is the execution address in the *SAVE command left at &0700, so this is the image's own entry point when it is *RUN, but nothing in this release reaches it.

subroutines.name: boot_loader_joystick
subroutines.title: Load the game file and run it (not used)
subroutines.description: Point BYTEV at joystick_bytev (&0780), then build an OSFILE control block at &6B00 naming boot_filename with load address &2000, call the filing system's FILEV handler to load the file, and jump to &2000. &0740 is the execution address in the *SAVE command left at &0700, so this is the image's own entry point when it is *RUN, but nothing in this release reaches it.

subroutines.name: coder_start
subroutines.title: Coder: load the game and the next level
subroutines.description:
Build the game afresh from disc for the next level and start it. Run once per level as *CODER: for the first level by *DUNJUNZ, and for each later one by next_level_intercept during the reset that ends the level before. It never returns.

Count the level: levels_started and level_digits, the filename's number ("1 " to "25"), live in page &08, which the reset leaves alone and *DUNJUNZ resets for a new game. Blank the display (6845 register 1 = 0) and silence the VDU, then *LOAD DUN1, which holds this code, so the bytes being run are rewritten with identical ones; the reload also restores level_command, so the digits go into it only afterwards. Load the level file to &6B00, which is screen memory: LEVELnn, or for level 25 STONES at &6680, whose last &2B0 bytes are level 25.

Copy one of the two &0400-&07FF images into place: the one with joystick_bytev only if ADC channel 1 reads with a high byte of exactly &80. The channel is read again to decide whether to point BYTEV at &0780, so if the two reads disagree the image and the vector do not match: the joystick image with the MOS's BYTEV, or BYTEV at the keyboard image's &0780, which holds zeros (BRK). Show 80 columns and 23 rows again (the level file's rows 23-24 stay hidden), then copy the game core: all of &3000-&473F to &08C0-&1FFF for the first level, but only from &3440, to &0D00-&1FFF, for later ones, so that the heroes' scores and attributes in &08C0-&0CFF carry over. Leave levels_started in &8E for game_entry, and jump to it.

Coder uses the game's zero page &70-&73 and &80-&81 for its pointers; nothing there is needed until game_entry.

subroutines.name: next_level_by_reset
subroutines.title: Move on to the next level by resetting the machine
subroutines.description: End a level that at least one hero survived, by having the machine reset itself into Coder. Reached through to_next_level, after level_loop's end has given the dead heroes their starting attributes back. Arm the MOS BREAK intercept (&0287-&0289) with a JMP to next_level_intercept and jump to the MOS 1.20 reset entry at &D9CD; the MOS calls the intercept during the reset, and its second call runs *CODER, which reloads the game and the next level. Page &08 (levels_started, level_digits and the menu's tables) and &08C0-&0CFF (the heroes' attributes and scores) survive the reset and Coder's copy. Never returns.

subroutines.name: restart_by_reset
subroutines.title: Restart the game by resetting the machine
subroutines.description: End the game after all four heroes have died. Reached from level_loop's end once the game-over message has been shown for up to 5.8 seconds. Arm the BREAK intercept with a JMP to restart_intercept and branch to reset_machine, so that the reset runs *DUNJUNZ, which resets page &08, shows the title screen and runs Coder for a new game. Never returns.

subroutines.name: restart_intercept
subroutines.title: BREAK intercept: reload the game
subroutines.description: Called twice by the MOS during the reset that restart_by_reset makes. The first call (carry clear) comes before the filing system is initialised and does nothing. On the second, clear the screen of the game-over message, select the disc filing system and *DUNJUNZ, which takes over and never returns.

on_entry.C: set on the second call, after the filing system is initialised

subroutines.name: next_level_intercept
subroutines.title: BREAK intercept: run Coder for the next level
subroutines.description: Called twice by the MOS during the reset that next_level_by_reset makes. The first call (carry clear) comes before the filing system is initialised and does nothing. On the second, select MODE 2, the disc filing system and *RUN CODER, which loads the next level and never returns. *DUNJUNZ also points the intercept at &15B5 while *CODER loads, so a BREAK then lands here too, but &15B5 holds this routine only if Coder has copied the game core there since power-on.

on_entry.C: set on the second call, after the filing system is initialised

subroutines.name: check_level
subroutines.title: Check the level and set the text window
subroutines.description:
Make the level Coder loaded ready for unpack_level. Called by start_level after clear_text_for_level: Coder has already put the file at &6B00-&6DAF. Decrypt it and check its checksum (decrypt_level resets the machine on a mismatch).

Then set the bottom row of clear_text_area's text window from 22 to 24. Dun1 stores it as 22, so that clear_text_for_level's clear stops at row 22, above the level file in rows 23-24; from here on the whole screen is cleared. Coder reloads Dun1 for each level, so the window is 22 again at the next level's start.

subroutines.name: joystick_bytev
subroutines.title: BYTEV handler: read a joystick for the Barbarian's keys
subroutines.description: Installed on BYTEV by Coder, in the joystick image of &0400-&07FF only. Answers test_key's OSBYTE &81 scans of the Barbarian's (hero 2's) keys from the analogue port, so that a joystick plays the Barbarian: left (. &98) and right (/ &97) from channel 1, up (K &B9) and down (, &99) from channel 2, and fire (SPACE &9D) from either fire button. A direction counts only at the stick's extreme, when the channel's high byte is &FF or 0, so the stick works as a switch. Every other call goes to the MOS 1.20 OSBYTE routine at &E772 directly, skipping any other BYTEV claimant. The handler's own OSBYTE &80 reads come back through BYTEV into it and are passed on the same way. The Barbarian's five keys are never scanned while it is installed, so that hero can be played only with the joystick. test_key counts a key as held only when X and Y both come back &FF, so a not-pressed answer needs only X = 0.

on_exit.X: &FF if the key is pressed, 0 if not

subroutines.name: clear_text_for_level
subroutines.title: Clear the text area before a level
subroutines.description: start_level's first call. Only clears the screen: no level number is shown, and level_number is not counted here (game_entry sets it from levels_started). At this point clear_text_area's window still ends at row 22, as Dun1 stores it, so the level file Coder loaded into rows 23-24 is kept for check_level; Dun1's other stored bytes in rows 0-22 are wiped.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Zero bytes, which nothing reads.

banners.name: hero_start_max_missiles
banners.title: Heroes' starting attributes
banners.description: Four tables of one byte per hero (Ranger, Magic-User, Barbarian, Fighter): missiles in flight, missile damage, health lost per hit, and the face sprite for the panel.

banners.name: game_over_message
banners.title: Game-over message
banners.description: Eleven lines of seventeen characters, each ended by a carriage return, then a line feed and a last line ended by a zero byte. Two bytes of it (&0FF1, &0FF2) double as counters, and are overwritten with spaces before printing, so the full stop after "YOU ALL" never appears.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes: "ND!" and a zero, the end of an earlier message, then "&C2".

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes, never read: &52 &78 &60 repeat the end of plot_chalice (JSR plot_at_cell's operand, then RTS), and the rest reads as a fragment of BASIC text, "(&1900+F".

banners.name: sprite_chalice
banners.title: The Chalice sprite
banners.description: Sprite &73: 8 bytes by 24 rows, two cells by two, plotted at x &1A, y 4 by plot_chalice. In the victory sequence dissolve_chalice zeros random bytes of it and erase_victory_ring zeros all of it (and the byte after); the game then ends in a reset.

banners.name: font_letters
banners.title: Font: letters A-Z
banners.description: Eight bytes per letter, copied into the definition of character 128 by the WRCHV handler.

banners.name: font_digits
banners.title: Font: digits 0-9
banners.description: Eight bytes per digit, copied into the definition of character 128 by the WRCHV handler.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes, never read: a second copy of the digit 9's eight glyph rows, then &74.

banners.title: restart_intercept's commands
banners.description: The *DISC and *DUNJUNZ command lines, read from &1489 and &148E (the C before DISC is not read). After them come stale bytes: STA &149C, LDA #&FF, JSR &3000, JMP &0450, the end of a level loader that calls FILEV's routine through a patched JSR.

banners.title: Unused, then next_level_intercept's commands
banners.description: Stale bytes, never run: &15D2-&15D8 repeat next_level_intercept's LDX #&E5, LDY #&15, JSR OSCLI, and an RTS and "ODER" follow. Then the *DISC and *RUN CODER command lines read from &15E0 and &15E5, and more unused bytes.

banners.name: view_frame_plots
banners.title: View frame PLOT commands
banners.description: Twenty five-byte VDU 25 commands (plot code, then x and y as 16-bit words) sent by draw_view_frames, five for each view's frame: PLOT 4 moves to the top-left corner, three PLOT 1s draw relative lines down 388, right 520 and up 388, and PLOT 5 draws back to the corner. The corners are (8,1022), (552,1022), (8,614) and (552,614); the second frame's first line is 389 long.

banners.name: sprite_sword_up
banners.title: Sword sprites
banners.description: Sprites &49-&4C, the Fighter's missile flying up, right, down and left: 4 bytes by 12 rows each.

banners.title: Unused
banners.description: Leftover bytes, never read, including fragments of BASIC text ("?&A66=(rx%-lx%)", "sprite%?&A99=by%-ty%+1").

banners.name: sprite_shield
banners.title: Panel sprites: the shield and the small digits
banners.description: Sprite &69, the shield beside each hero's face in the status panel (3 bytes by 12 rows), then sprites &6A-&72, the small digits 1-9 (1 byte by 5 rows), which show the armour rating on the shield and the missile damage.

banners.name: sprite_missile_icon
banners.title: Panel sprites: the missile and boots icons
banners.description: Sprite &74, the missile icon, one per missile a hero may have in flight (4 bytes by 3 rows), and sprite &75, the boots icon shown while a hero wears the Boots of Speed (2 bytes by 6 rows).

banners.name: workspace_template
banners.title: Workspace template
banners.description: The starting contents of page &0D, the heroes' and missiles' workspace, which reset_workspace copies there whole at the start of every level. Byte +n becomes &0D00 + n. It sets the heroes in the four cells of the start, facing four ways and not stepping; every missile slot empty; each hero's direction and fire keys (hero_key_up etc. at +&70, as negative INKEY numbers for test_key); health digits 9 and 9 + 1 (+&90, +&95), which read 99 once draw_status_panel has taken a point; every view on the start room (+&A0); the heroes' and missiles' sprite bases (+&B0, +&B5); the bit masks test_wall and test_object_free use (+&C0); and the panel rows (+&D0). The bytes between variables are copied with the rest.

memory_map.name: hero_score_ten_thousands

memory_map.name: hero_absent
memory_map.description: One flag per hero: 1 if switched off on the menu, 0 if playing. hero_menu toggles it with keys 1-4; remove_absent_heroes takes the absent heroes out of play at each level.

memory_map.name: levels_started
memory_map.description: The level being played, 1-25, counted as levels started in this game. It lives in page &08, which survives the reset between levels: *DUNJUNZ sets it to 0 for a new game and coder_start adds one before loading each level. coder_start also reads it to choose Stones for level 25, to copy the whole game core only for level 1, and to pass it to game_entry in level_count_copy; game_entry and level_loop read it for the first-level test and the monsters' hit points.

memory_map.name: level_digits
memory_map.description: The level number as ASCII digits for the level's filename: one digit and a space ("1 "-"9 "), or two digits ("10"-"25"). *DUNJUNZ sets "0 "; coder_start advances it before each level, in page &08 across the reset, and copies it into level_command_digits.
